citations.desc: Access and inspection of records and property; submission of itineraries.
citations.narrative:
A responsible adult was not available to accompany APHIS Officials during the inspection process at 11:24am on June
25, 2026. The inspector attempted to contact the licensee by calling and texting the phone numbers on file. Failure to
provide access to the facility, animals, and records for inspection is a violation of the AWA and regulations. Continued
failure to provide access is serious and may result in enforcement action.

citations.desc: Access and inspection of records and property; submission of itineraries.
citations.narrative:
An unannounced, routine inspection was attempted at 11:24 am on June 25, 2026. A responsible adult was not available
to accompany APHIS Officials during the inspection process. Phone calls were not immediately answered; however, a
requested return call was received at 1:45 pm. The licensee stated that he was traveling and exhibiting his animals out of
state. A written itinerary was not submitted by the licensee prior to exhibiting with overnight travel.
Itineraries are necessary to allow for the inspection of traveling exhibitors to confirm compliance with the Animal Welfare
Act, notably regarding the animal care and welfare while traveling.
The licensee must submit a written itinerary to the Deputy Administrator no fewer than two days in advance of any travel
and shall contain complete and accurate information concerning the whereabouts of any animal intended for exhibition at
any location other than the person’s approved site. To be corrected from this date, June 25, 2026, forward.
End Section
